I was looking at this fairly recent paper:
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33510387/
and I think we could maybe add improved MF annotations for several proteins in this paper, as the currently available experimental MF annotations are not optimal:
MSH2 and MSH6 (MutSalpha complex) could be annotated to “ATP-dependent DNA damage sensor activity”
PMS1 and MLH1 (MutLalpha complex) could be annotated to “DNA endonuclease activity”

Would that be fairly straightforward to do, using the new functionality for adding new experimental annotations?

* **Type of Issue: Erroneous source or erroneous propagation, or other issue**

* Add the label 'high priority' if needed. Generally high priority issues affect a lot of proteins, and annotations are incorrect (as opposed to just imprecise).
title: PAINT issue: potential new MF annotations for some mismatch repair proteins

author: marcfeuermann
body:
Hello Paul, 
Thank you for this information. I must say that the functions of the various Mut complexes are sometimes difficult to understand. This is not made any easier by the fact that there are distinct complexes with different sub-units. This paper provides some clarity. Thank you for providing me with the reference. It's so much easier when I know where to look. I made the annotations as you requested. Since these are complexes, I added the CONTRIBUTES_TO tag. This allows MF binding terms to be replaced with more appropriate functional terms.
I was tempted to annotate the terms at the roots of the PTHR11361 and PTHR10073 families, but it is better to remain cautious and for the moment only annotate the sub-units of the MutL-alpha and MutS-alpha complexes. I will come back to the others if I find similar evidence.
Since we moved on to the family review phase, I've been using the primary annotation tool a lot... it makes a real difference in improving the quality of family annotation.
Cheers,
Marc.
